newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B index ends higher on interim optimism.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends higher on interim optimism.

text.p: Shenzhen's B shares ended with solid gains on Monday as the recent sharp rally extended on an optimistic outlook for 1997 interim company results, analysts said.

The Hong Kong dollar-denominated B share index gained 1.88 points or 1.42 percent to 134.25 on turnover of HK$72.7 million compared with HK$87.8 million last Friday. The A share index rose 12.80 points or 3.21 percent to 411.02 on turnover of 7.8 billion yuan against 5.6 billion yuan in the previous session.
"We are expecting some positive interim reports," an analyst at J&A Securities (HK) said.
With the heat of the company reporting season approaching, analysts said investors would focus on firms seen offering good interim dividends.
Some analysts said they expected more gains on Tuesday despite profit-taking, judging from rises on both the A and B indices in the last few minutes of trading on Monday.
"The A and B share markets still have the strength to climb given the strong rises during the last minutes of trading today," the J&A analyst said.
Investors also felt the anti-speculation policies, which have affected the markets since May, were quietening down, analysts said.

People saw less likelihood that the government would take further immediate measures to cool the markets after Beijing formally announced on Friday that Zhou Zhengqing had taken over as head of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC).
The CSRC leadership change was seen as one of the last in a series of government moves to curb stock speculation, analysts said.
But some analysts said the B share market was likely to fall because the rally, which began last Thursday after hitting a 1997 low of 120.44 points a day earlier, was running out of steam.
"I think the B share technical rebound is coming to an end as there is no solid news to drive it," an analyst at China Securities said.
Refrigerator maker Hefei Meiling Co Ltd was the sharpest winner in the B share market, soaring HK$0.37 or 8.01 percent to HK$4.99.
Recently-listed Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd was one of the most heavily traded stocks on volume of 3.1 million shares, gaining HK$0.25 to HK$7.70.
In the A share market, Tangshan Iron & Steel was one of the top gainers, rising 1.15 yuan to its 10 percent limit-up at 12.64 yuan.
